resources.string: No NFC feature, adapter, HAL or kernel driver: nothing to test.
NFC is declared without host card emulation: android.hardware.nfc.hce.xml is missing, so payment and transit apps cannot emulate cards.

The kernel or init shows an NFC controller but FEATURE_NFC is not declared: android.hardware.nfc.xml is missing from vendor/etc/permissions, so the NFC service never starts and Settings has no NFC switch.
FEATURE_NFC is declared but there is no NfcAdapter: com.android.nfc is not installed or crashed at start, often because the NFC HAL or its config (libnfc-nci.conf, libnfc-nxp.conf) is missing.
Turn NFC on in Settings and run again. If the switch turns itself off, the HAL could not initialise the controller (firmware download, wrong config file, I2C or GPIO problem).
An NFC service is restarting in a loop: the HAL crashes while talking to the controller. Check its tombstones and logcat (NfcHal, NxpHal, libnfc).
An NFC driver is registered on I2C but no device is bound to it: the probe failed. Check the device tree node (I2C address, interrupt, enable and firmware GPIOs, clock request) and dmesg.
FEATURE_NFC is declared but no NFC properties, services or device nodes are visible to apps (SELinux). Not a fault by itself.
A tag was detected but its UID or technology list is empty: the controller reports incomplete activation data.
NFC is off: turn it on in Settings.
UID, technologies, ATQA/SAK and NDEF records
The reader needs the app window in the foreground.
Hold a tag, a contactless card or a transit card against the back of the phone, near the NFC antenna.
The tag was detected but could not be decoded.
A successful read is saved as a result automatically. Only data the tag gives without authentication is read; nothing is written.
